Legend still shows Latest / Peak / Total (Grafana's built-in lastNotNull / max / sum reducers -- rendered as "Last *" / "Max" / "Total"). Each model and fleet total reconciles to native spend. Aggregated with max_over_time, not increase: these counters are cumulative PER SESSION (every series carries session_id) and expire 15m after their last sample, so increase() would treat a short session's first sample as its baseline and undercount. Legend now shows Latest / Peak / Total (Grafana's built-in lastNotNull / max / sum reducers -- Grafana does not allow renaming a legend calc's own column header, so the table literally reads "Last *" / "Max" / "Total"). Total is now a legitimate window sum, not the double-counting bug OTL-82 originally fixed. Measured live against the stat tile's raw total for the same window (job="otel-collector", no template-var filtering, $__interval=2m over a live 2h window, real fleet churn): tokens matched within about 3-4% (undercount); cost was off by roughly 6-15% depending on bucket width (overcount, worse at narrow buckets, improving toward ~6% by 10-15m buckets) -- not a tight guarantee, the honest tolerance for this construction on a live, high-churn multi-session dataset. See the PR thread for the full numbers and the alternatives that were tried and rejected (a wide-window aggregate delta undercounted by ~17-20%).

panels.title: ⑤ Provider Lanes (Claude · GLM · Codex · Qwen)
panels.description: OTL-81: cross-provider rollup. Claude + GLM ride the same claude_code_* metric family (GLM identified by model=~"^glm" — verified live 2026-08-24 this account carries NO `account` label, contradicting the ticket's account="glm-coding" assumption; use the model regex, not account). Codex (openai) emits its own codex_* metric family / service_name=codex_exec, no real cost telemetry. Qwen not yet emitting (OTL-80 tracks the qwencloud CLI wiring) — structural placeholder only, see the text panel below and the ai:tokens:sum{provider="qwen"} recording-rule leg in provisioning/prometheus/recording-rules.yml.

panels.description: OTL-80 authoritative first-party rates (docs.z.ai/guides/overview/pricing, fetched 2026-08-24): GLM-5.3 = $1.40/M input, $0.26/M cached-input, $4.40/M output, no separate cache-write fee (writes bill at the input rate). Applied uniformly to every model=~"^glm.*" series on this account (5.3-only rate — 5-turbo/4.7 price differently per OTL-80, follow-up to split by model). This is the TRUSTWORTHY GLM dollar figure — use this, never the raw claude_code_cost_usage_USD_total for a glm model (see the panel beside this one).

panels.description: DO NOT report this number as GLM spend. Claude Code prices GLM sessions from its own Anthropic-protocol cost table, which OTL-80 measured at ~2.8x the true metered-equivalent rate on a probe request (~2.3x measured live against this dashboard's own 7d window 2026-08-24: $48.54 raw vs $20.92 rerated). Shown here ONLY so the gap between raw and rerated is visible side by side — the panel to the left is the number to use.

panels.title: Tokens by Provider (Claude · GLM · Codex)
panels.description: Cross-provider token volume via the ai:tokens:sum canonical recording rule (provisioning/prometheus/recording-rules.yml): provider=anthropic (real Claude, model!~"^glm"), provider=glm (model=~"^glm", split out 2026-08-24 for OTL-81), provider=openai (Codex_Desktop/app-server native token metric only — codex_exec headless emits no Prometheus token-usage series, see the recording-rules.yml header note). provider=qwen is a structural placeholder — its series appear automatically once Qwen telemetry exists (OTL-80). OTL-82-r4 (Ryan-directed redesign): each point is now the amount accrued IN THAT INTERVAL BUCKET, not a running total -- computed per-series as clamp_min(this bucket's max - the previous bucket's max, 0), summed across series (avoids increase()/rate(), which this repo's OTL-75 note already flagged as unreliable on these per-session counters -- max_over_time keeps that guarantee, applied per-bucket instead of over a growing window). Legend now shows Latest / Peak / Total (Grafana's built-in lastNotNull / max / sum reducers -- Grafana does not allow renaming a legend calc's own column header, so the table literally reads "Last *" / "Max" / "Total"). Total is now a legitimate window sum, not the double-counting bug OTL-82 originally fixed. Measured live against the stat tile's raw total for the same window (job="otel-collector", no template-var filtering, $__interval=2m over a live 2h window, real fleet churn): tokens matched within about 3-4% (undercount); cost was off by roughly 6-15% depending on bucket width (overcount, worse at narrow buckets, improving toward ~6% by 10-15m buckets) -- not a tight guarantee, the honest tolerance for this construction on a live, high-churn multi-session dataset. See the PR thread for the full numbers and the alternatives that were tried and rejected (a wide-window aggregate delta undercounted by ~17-20%).

panels.title: Real + Rerated Spend by Provider (Claude · GLM)

options.content:
### Claude Code emits no metric this section could plot

A tok/s **percentile distribution** per model (mirroring the Latency section above) needs a per-request pairing of *tokens generated* and *time taken*, exposed as a histogram Grafana can run `histogram_quantile()` against. Checked the full live `claude_code_*` metric surface (2026-08-25) -- it does not exist:

- `claude_code_api_request_duration_seconds_bucket` -- a duration histogram, labeled `model`/`le`. No token count attached to any one request.
- `claude_code_token_usage_tokens_total` -- a counter, labeled `model`/`type` (input/output/cacheRead/cacheCreation). No duration attached, and it is a *cumulative counter*, not a per-request event -- there is no way to recover "tokens produced in the same request that took N seconds" from it.

These two metrics are never joined at the per-request level anywhere in the exported telemetry, so there is no way to derive a real percentile distribution of tokens/second from what's on this stack today -- only a coarse aggregate (`rate(tokens_total) / rate(duration_seconds_sum)` over a window), which is a single blended number, not a P50-P99 distribution, and would misrepresent the ticket's ask if shown here as if it were one.

**What would light this up:** Claude Code's OTel exporter would need to either (a) emit a genuine per-request `tokens_per_second` (or `output_tokens` + `duration`) histogram, or (b) attach an output-token count as an attribute on the same span/event that already carries `api_request_duration`, so the two can be correlated per-request instead of only as independent aggregates. Neither exists in the current Claude Code telemetry surface -- this is an upstream instrumentation gap, not something this dashboard's queries can work around.

panels.description: Tokens consumed per time bucket, grouped by normalized model family and summed across input, output, cache-read, and cache-creation token classes. Aggregated with max_over_time, not increase: these counters are cumulative PER SESSION (every series carries session_id) and expire 15m after their last sample, so increase() would treat a short session's first sample as its baseline and undercount. See OTL-75. OTL-83 / OTL-82 recording-rules round (Ryan-directed): Ryan independently confirmed these 'by Host'/'by Model' panels were never meant to be cumulative -- the per-interval redesign in the primary section above (same title, no 'Cumulative' prefix) is correct and stays primary. This panel is an OPTIONAL secondary view, collapsed by default, offering the cumulative/running-total reading for whoever wants it. No longer built from a query-time max_over_time($__range) window (OTL-82-r3's shape, which matched the true total exactly at the FINAL point but could still dip mid-chart under session churn -- OTL-83). Now reads directly from the same monotonic, forward-latching recording rule the per-interval panels use (ai:tokens_accum:sum / ai:cost_usd_accum:sum -- see provisioning/prometheus/recording-rules.yml's "ai-canonical-running-total" group), anchored to the dashboard's own start via `@ ${__from:date:seconds}` (closes the earlier Codex P1 finding -- no pre-loaded first point). Because the underlying series is monotonic non-decreasing by construction (each 1m tick can only take the max of its prior recorded value and what it just observed), accum(t) - accum(@ start) is GENUINELY unable to decrease as t advances -- not merely measured to dip less often. Do not conflate this number with the per-interval panel of the same base title above -- they answer different questions (growth-since-window-start vs amount-in-this-bucket) and will not match.
